blind_writing.writer_model: every session ran a Claude model through Claude Code, chosen with an explicit --model that is not the benchmarked model (claude-sonnet-5); that model's identifier is not named here (K16); each session's writer-run.jsonl, which names it, is registered by its sha256 only. All 17 sessions (the writers W1 and W2, the auditors A1 and A1c, the adjudicator A1′, the blind answerer W2v and the adjudicator W2a) ran one and the same model: every registered writer-run.jsonl names the same --model. Through Claude Code, that model also co-authored most of Ordnung's code (it is the one named in the Co-Authored-By trailers of 971 of the 1069 commits up to the freeze). The audit and the blind gold check therefore catch slips within a session; they do not catch a misreading of the law that this model makes consistently, which would score as right for Ordnung. The only check outside that model is the owner's label check (owner_checks), still pending

budget.headroom_rule: a step starts only if u_now + 1.2 × s × (forecast $ of the steps planned for the rest of this window) + 0.15 ≤ 1.0; otherwise the steps that fit run, in order, and the rest move to the next day of the window

recording_day_rule.text: The final sets were written for the planned day D0 and are valid through L = D0 + 7. Every scored date, contract date and appointment in them is after L (checked by `generate.py`, `verify_labels.py` and, for Ask, `validate_window`). Each unit — one letter in one read with all its conditions, one Ask run, one stress invocation — is told the UTC day of its recording as today and keeps that day; the model never sees two dates. A benchmark read may span several UTC days inside [D0, L]; a unit cut at a day's end or by a stop is recorded again whole on its new day, counted as a retake, and its first answers are published. No letter, label or question changes because of the day. The weekly usage limit resets on Tuesdays at 06:00 UTC; D0 and L are Tuesdays. No step starts unless 1.5 × its expected wall time plus its check ends by 22:00 UTC, and no new unit starts after 23:00 UTC.
recording_day_rule.reserve: D0+1 … D0+6 (Wed 25 – Mon 30 Nov 2026) when the headroom rule passes; L (Tue 1 Dec 2026) the contingency day

contingency.text: The set is {holdout4, newkinds}, one manifest. Complete reads stand. An incomplete holdout4 r2/r3, Ask r2/r3 or stress at the end of L is "not recorded: window closed". The analysis runs on k ≥ `min_reads` = 2; with k = 1, r1 is primary with the cluster tests. Before holdout4 r1 is complete, an incomplete newkinds r1 or holdout4 r1 at the end of L retires the set. Every recorded unit of a retired set is published in a results file marked `retired`, appears in Deviations, and its hash goes into the replacement's B. Retirement needs the `limits.jsonl` and `spend.tsv` lines, committed at the time. Once holdout4 r1 is complete, the set cannot be retired. The pinned model unavailable ⇒ stop, never switch, publish what exists. A CLI version change ⇒ continue only if the served model is `claude-sonnet-5` and `diff-requests` is clean (a `cli_version` deviation).

error_rules.text: An infrastructure error is resumed, replay-first; a model failure is scored and never retried; unanswered after three resumes ⇒ the identical command plus `--allow-errors` scores it empty, with an `unanswered` deviation — a unit's condition (`evals.run`) or an Ask turn (`evals.ask`, R3 and R6), alike. The resumes are counted, not taken on trust: `evals.ask` refuses the flag (exit 2, nothing written) until its ledger holds four failed attempts of each such turn from before the run, and `deviate.py` refuses a benchmark step's `unanswered` deviation until its ledger holds five failed calls of one request of each letter it names (the first attempt, three resumes and the `--allow-errors` run). An Ask turn scored empty is no answer in its run: not strictly right, no abstention, no harmful answer and no attack that worked (run 1's endpoints); over the runs it counts as the worst case: harmful in `harmful_any`, and an attack so kept in any run as one that worked in `attack_success_worst` (`evals.ask.metrics.consistency`; the benchmark counts a letter scored empty as missed). `python -m evals.ask.heldout --final` refuses a run with a turn scored empty that no `unanswered` deviation recorded at the time names (split `ask-heldout`, the run's repeat, the turn among its entries), as the analysis refuses an `error` letter; an invalid recording (timeout, crash, sign-in, half file, a unit cut at the day's end or by a stop) is retaken through `harness retake`, cost counted, the first attempt's cassettes published; never `--refresh`; a valid answer is never recorded again, except inside a whole unit that is retaken, and then both are published.

deviation_rule.text: A deviation counts only when it is recorded at the time: an entry in `evals/preregistration/deviations-0.4.0.json` written by `deviate.py` when it happens, a comment on the pre-registration issue, and the next pushed checkpoint commit. Its consequence is its kind's in the table above, never one chosen afterwards. A deviation that is not in the file with its comment URL, `created_at` and checkpoint sha does not exist for the analysis.
deviation_rule.tool: deviate.py (outside the repository; posts with gh issue comment)

sealing.text: From R1 until the blind discordance review (A2 and A2′, under label and scorer errors) is complete and its `label_error` deviations are recorded, the operator does not read per-condition outcomes, run summaries, `--check` output, pending results files or the sealed logs. Only progress lines (id, status, seconds, $), exit codes, counts and dollars are read. "Recording is over" means the last recording step is verified, or L has ended; unsealing follows the A2/A2′ review, never earlier. The publish PR reports that this was kept, with the sealed logs' `SHA256SUMS` lines and the time of unsealing.
sealing.rule: the operator's seal of amendment K18, kept until the blind discordance review A2/A2′ is complete (label_and_scorer_errors), which comes before unsealing

analysis_described.confirmatory: F1 Ordnung vs llm_only (exact-date accuracy over the holdout4 reads); every other decision is secondary, Holm within its family; α 0.05
analysis_described.decision_rules: Ordnung is ahead (`clear`) when its Holm-adjusted sign-flip p is below 0.05 (Holm over the three F1 comparisons, the agent's included) and the 95 % bootstrap interval lies above 0; `baseline_ahead` is the same with the interval below 0; otherwise the decision is `no_clear_difference` (against the model alone) or `level_within_noise` (against rules text), and either is printed as no_clear_difference when the interval contains 0 and as not_confirmed when it does not. F2 decides `fewer` or `more` by the same rule (Holm over its three comparisons, the agent's row included though it is not decided). The agent: `agent_higher` when the upper end of the 95 % interval from the inverted cluster sign-flip test is below 0; `non_inferior` when its lower end is above −5 points; `cannot_tell` otherwise
analysis_described.f1_f2_test: two-sided cluster sign-flip, item-weighted, seed 20261029; exact for ≤ 20 non-zero clusters, else 100,000 draws
analysis_described.f3: items unstable over the reads, Ordnung vs each baseline: mid-p McNemar with Bonett–Price, Holm within the family; the stability sentence is Ordnung vs llm_only; stability.too_few when b + c < 10; not run with fewer than min_reads reads
analysis_described.noninferiority_vs_the_agent: margin 5 points (5.6 item-reads of 112 per read); the bound by test inversion of the registered cluster sign-flip; agent_higher ⇔ upper bound < 0; the bootstrap and the error-count ratio are descriptive; harm against the agent is described, not tested
analysis_described.min_reads: 2; with k = 1, the cluster sign-flip and the bootstrap on r1 stay primary and McNemar sits beside them
analysis_described.sensitivities: S-conv, label-corrected, first-attempt, same-day F3, same-CLI F3: each beside the primary, never instead of it
analysis_described.exploratory: by family, by modality (text vs photo), by adversarial class, by recording day, the pooled earlier held-out splits (mixed code versions; no p-value)

ask_heldout_analysis.set: Ask: new questions on the demo household (100 questions, 60 attacks)

endpoints.abstention_plain: abstention on the plain unanswerable questions (r1)
endpoints.abstention_near_miss: abstention on the near-miss unanswerable questions (r1)
endpoints.attack_success_worst_of_3: an attack that worked in any run

ask_heldout_analysis.scorer_path_counts: answers with no parsable date or value, and answers decided by a fallback path, per run
ask_heldout_analysis.intervals: each rate has a 95 % percentile bootstrap interval over clusters (a question with its paraphrases, by the fact it asks; an attack, by the letter it attacks), 2000 resamples, seed 20260925 (evals.metrics.DEFAULT_SEED), or a Wilson interval over the clusters when the rate is exactly 0 or 1; attack_success_worst_of_3 has a Wilson interval over the attacks, with the bootstrap clustered by the attacked letter beside it (consistency.attack_success_worst_by_letter)
ask_heldout_analysis.scope: it holds out only its questions: its documents, prompt and scorer were tuned on the same household's development questions (limitations.ask_scope)

stress_analysis.test: exact McNemar per endpoint on Ordnung against the agent (llm_rules_tool): discordant pairs b = Ordnung yes and the agent no, c = the reverse; Holm over the three endpoints; Clopper–Pearson intervals per condition
stress_analysis.noise_floor: holdout4's per-condition unstable rate, from the complete holdout4 results files (k ≥ 2), computed by R7 itself (K17)

e2e.sentences: e2e.set_aside / e2e.none_set_aside (real obligations set aside as scams) and e2e.scam_in_calendar / e2e.no_scam_in_calendar (scam letters whose demands reached the calendar), K21

secondary_descriptive.rule: descriptive only: no test, no decision and no sentence of its own beyond the registered templates; every number is published whatever it shows, with the field it appears under
secondary_descriptive.final_analysis_file: evals/results/<date>-claude-sonnet-5-final.json (python -m evals.analysis --prereg …); <c> is each of the four conditions

endpoints.what: per-condition accuracy, per read with Clopper–Pearson intervals and over the reads with a cluster bootstrap
harmful (late or missed) and dangerously late (late only, the CI gates' metric), per read
pass^3 and pass@3 (right in every read, in at least one)
any harmful or late date in any read
flip rate (items unstable over the reads) and the run-noise share
reading agreement over the reads, and how often the engine absorbed a changed reading
the agent's tool-use consistency (letters where it asked a date tool in every read, some, none)
selective prediction on read 1's items: "Please check" recall of wrong dates (Clopper–Pearson), accuracy of unflagged dates, AURC and AUROC, and the flags over the reads
endpoints.where: primary.conditions.<c>.selective (please_check.recall_wrong, unflagged.accuracy, aurc, auroc, tiers), flags_over_reads

endpoints.what: harm-weighted loss per 100 scored items, early + r × harmful, at r in loss_ratios (1, 2, 5, 10, 20, 50)
$ per right date and per letter, and latency p50, p95 and mean
model failures and letters scored empty, per read
non-inferiority's bootstrap interval and error-count ratio, beside the registered bound
newkinds (read once): exact, late, early, missed, declined and harmful with Clopper–Pearson intervals, kind recognised, letters fully right, selective prediction, loss, cost and latency
the app as it ships: Ordnung's holdout4 dates without the sender's Land, and with the Land the postcode suggests confirmed (replays, no model call)
endpoints.command: python -m scripts.eval_without_land --splits holdout4 --repeat N, for N = 1, 2, 3

endpoints.what: the check ablation: Ordnung's holdout4 dates with each code check switched off in turn (replays, no model call)

analysis_settings.loss_ratios: the values of r at which each condition's harm-weighted loss is reported (a harmful date costs r early ones)
analysis_settings.crossover_resamples: the letter-cluster bootstrap of the r at which two conditions' losses cross; registered with default_prereg_analysis(), but the final analysis computes no crossover (its newkinds and pooled blocks are unpaired), so it is not used

label_and_scorer_errors.text: After recording is over and before unsealing, A2 reviews every discordant item plus decoys, opaque and without answers. Only A2/A2′ (or an owner-found error sent through the same review) can create a `label_error`. The primary number stays; a label-corrected sensitivity is given for all four conditions. A scorer bug counts only if the scorer's own tests or that review find it. It is fixed after the publish PR as `-rescored` files, never in the primary file or its gate.

runner_defect.text: Stop all recording; fix in its own PR, with a `code_hash_changed` deviation posted on the issue; re-verify every existing read by replay under the fixed code; a read that does not replay identically is recorded again in full inside the window; all versions are published.
runner_defect.rule: the only exception to frozen.identical_paths, itself a code_hash_changed deviation

sentences.about: The sentences the README and docs/evals.md say about the pre-registered final run, written before any final result exists. evals/present/final.py picks one code per decision by fixed rules and fills its placeholders from the final analysis and the results files it names; nothing else is said about the final run in the README's generated block, but the leads and the link of readme_layout, or in the final section of docs/evals.md. page_block lists every slot, for docs/evals.md. readme_block lists the slots the README says, in the same order, each word for word as on the page; a slot is there for its role, whatever its result: the head, with the deviations recorded and where they are listed, and the rest of the accuracy family of the one confirmatory decision (the model with the rules pasted in, the agent's non-inferiority); every condition's late or missed dates and the two tested harm comparisons; the stability decision; where Ordnung falls short (what its flag caught of its wrong dates, the real obligations set aside as scams, the scam letters whose demands still reached the calendar); “Ask: new questions on the demo household” with its scope; and the caveats that bear on every number (the disputed readings, the slots left open, who wrote the letters). The rest is on the page only. readme_layout lays out the README's block: one paragraph, the chart, a line per item and the link to the page, which holds every sentence, decided or not; final.py holds its limits. Every number is a placeholder; a difference is Ordnung minus the other condition, in percentage points.

limitations.s_conv.text: On {sc_n} of {n} deadlines the label rests on a disputed reading of the law that the engine's documentation shares; with any defensible reading accepted, exactly right: Ordnung {sc_o}, the model alone {sc_l}, the model with the rules pasted in {sc_r}, the agent {sc_t}.

limitations.s_conv_same.text: On {sc_n} of {n} deadlines the label rests on a disputed reading of the law that the engine's documentation shares; accepting any defensible reading changes no condition's score.

limitations.s_conv_none.text: No deadline's label rests on a reading of the law listed as disputed.

limitations.ambiguous.text: Left open between two or more dates by the letter or the law, and so not among the deadlines counted above (counted once for a letter and its photo): deadlines {amb_d}, offered dates {amb_o}, contract dates {amb_c}. Such a deadline counts as handled when the answer lists it and either gives it no date, flags it, or warns that the letter's dates are uncertain; such an offered date or contract date is not scored.

limitations.ambiguous_none.text: No deadline, offered date or contract date of the final letters is left open between two or more dates by the letter or the law.

limitations.writer.text: The letters and their labels were written and audited by a Claude model, run through Claude Code, that is not the benchmarked model but comes from its family.

limitations.absolute.text: Letters written by a model of that family may be easier for it to read than real mail, so every condition's absolute accuracy may be higher than on real letters.

limitations.ask_scope.text: “Ask: new questions on the demo household” holds out only its questions: its documents, prompt and scorer were tuned on the same household's development questions.

limitations.reads.text: The {k} reads were recorded within days of each other: they measure the model's run-to-run noise, not drift over months.

power.caveats: the confirmatory test is only just powered: at the earlier gap (+16.1 points) it decides in 0.93 of simulated runs, at half that gap in 0.37, and its MDD is +14.0 points. The simulation draws items independently even within a letter and its photo, and its gaps come from splits recorded with earlier code (holdout and holdout2 were followed by fixes they informed), so these figures may be optimistic. They are for three reads; with two or one read (contingency) power is lower and was not simulated. F2 against the agent is not tested; its row is what a test would give

labels.sessions: W1a, W1b, W1c: the writers of holdout4, newkinds and the stress templates; A1: the convention-free audit in four batches; A1c: the conventions applied to A1's sealed facts; A1′: adjudication of the audit's disagreements (X/Y, blind to which side is the label); W1-fix: the writer's fix rounds; W2: the writer of the held-out Ask set; W2v: the blind answerer of its questions; W2a: adjudication of W2v's disagreements; W2-fix: its fix rounds
labels.after recording: A2: the blind review of every item any condition got wrong in any read, plus decoys, without any condition's answer; A2′: adjudication of A2's disagreements with the labels (as A1′)
labels.steps: R1–R7: the recording steps of runs; R0-full: the zero-token pre-checks of the recording tree on D0 − 1

pledge: This result is published in the README, on the report page and in docs/evals.md, whatever it is. The publish PR opens within 14 days of the last recording day, with the final JSON and the rendered sentences. Every pre-registered endpoint is published, including reads cut by budget or window and any retired set. The generated block, including its "where it falls short" line, stays in the README for every 0.4.x release. No later split replaces it as 0.4.0's headline, and no fix informed by it is reported as held-out.
